Exact feasibility check with Z3

Source: R/integration-z3r.R
opt_z3_check.Rd

Translates the constraints and bounds of a linear model (LP or MILP, after parameter substitution) to linear integer and real arithmetic and asks Z3 whether a feasible point exists. For these theories Z3 is a decision procedure, so "sat" and "unsat" are exact answers about the model as written, without floating-point tolerances. A satisfying assignment is a feasible point, not an optimal one.

Usage

opt_z3_check(
  model,
  objective_bound = NULL,
  coefficients = c("decimal", "binary")
)

Arguments

model

An opt_model() with linear constraints.

objective_bound

Optional number: also require the objective to be at most (minimization) or at least (maximization) this value.

coefficients

"decimal" or "binary", see Details.

Value

A list with status ("sat", "unsat" or "unknown") and, when satisfiable, values, a named feasible point.

Details

Coefficients and bounds are doubles. With coefficients = "decimal" each is read as its 15-significant-digit decimal (so 0.1 means 1/10); with "binary" as the exact binary value of the double.

See also

opt_z3_certify()

Examples

m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", type = "integer", lower = 0, upper = 10)
opt_constraint(m, 2 * x == 7)
opt_z3_check(m)$status
#> [1] "unsat"
